title: Death ruled natural after stay in police cells
subtitle: The death of a man who died in hospital after a night in Saanich police cells has been classified as natural by a B.C. Coroners Service inquest. André Claude Boucher, 60, died Aug. 7, 2016, after several days in hospital.
article: The death of a man who died in hospital after a night in Saanich police cells has been classified as natural by a B.C. Coroners Service inquest.

André Claude Boucher, 60, died Aug. 7, 2016, after several days in hospital. He was taken to Victoria General Hospital on July 28, after spending the night in police cells. He had been monitored during the night and it was determined in the morning that further care was needed.
The report from the inquest, held from Monday to Wednesday at the Victoria courthouse, said the immediate cause of death was a brain hemorrhage due to a ruptured cerebral artery aneurysm.
On July 27, 2016, a Saanich resident called police after seeing Boucher stumbling over neighbours' lawns. During the incident, Boucher stepped off a 2.5-metre drop and fell onto concrete.

Saanich police Const. Mark Pamminger arrived on the scene and decided to take Boucher to cells after hearing that he lived alone. Pamminger told the inquest that he was concerned for Boucher's safety.

The inquest jury heard that Boucher was addicted to cocaine and alcohol, and had just begun to receive treatment for hepatitis C. A letter sent by his sister said he had been in a coma for eight days in 1977 after a car crash.
A coroner's inquest looks at details related to an unusual death but does not determine blame or guilt.
